Configure ArcheRage before installing Raid Framer:
1. Press ESC and open Options -> Game Info.
2. Enable "Enable Combat Messages".
3. Change the message range from SELF to ALL.
4. Set the message distance to 100 meters.
5. Close ArcheRage completely before continuing.

Raid Framer works best when ArcheRage is running in windowed mode.

1. Download the MSI installer and double-click it to run.\n2. When installation finishes, launch Raid Framer once from the Windows Start Menu. On first launch, Raid Framer copies its Lua addon into your ArcheRage/Addon folder.\n3. After Raid Framer has opened at least once, launch ArcheRage.

Whenever you want to record a PvP battle, launch Raid Framer from the Windows Start Menu. In the in-game addon, press the + button to start a new session. Combat data will appear while a session is active.
On the character select screen, open the wrench (tools) menu and confirm that "raidframer" appears in the addon list. It should be checked by default.

If no combat data appears, check:
• ESC -> Options -> Game Info: Enable Combat Messages is enabled.
• The message range is ALL, not SELF.
• The message distance is 100 meters.
• You pressed the + button in the addon to start a session.
• You completely restarted ArcheRage after installing Raid Framer.
• You opened the Raid Framer desktop app at least once after installation.
If RF2 is already installed, launching your existing Raid Framer installation should offer an update when one is available. You normally do not need to download the MSI manually again.

If everything else fails, close Raid Framer and delete this folder to reset its local settings and database:\nC:\\Users\\<YourWindowsUsername>\\.RaidFramer\\\nReplace <YourWindowsUsername> with your Windows account name. Deleting this folder removes Raid Framer's saved local settings and database, so the app will start fresh next time it is opened.

A 100-meter message distance can reduce performance when many players are nearby. Lowering the distance slider can reduce the hit, but also reduces the maximum distance of recorded events. If performance is still poor, choose a narrower message range such as SELF, PARTY, RAID, or GUILD instead of ALL to limit the events the game sends.

Control which features are active to improve FPS in large-scale battles. Disabling features reduces the amount of data processed per combat event.

You can also adjust event detection range directly in-game via ESC \u2192 Options \u2192 Game Info. The in-game combat settings (ESC → Options → Game Info) control what data flows into the addon.

“Show Combat Messages” checkbox: Toggles damage/heal hitsplats in the game visually, but does NOT affect data flow to the addon. You can have them on or off.

Info Filter (SELF / PARTY / RAID / GUILD / ALL): This DOES affect data flow. Changing the filter limits which combat events the addon receives.

Distance Slider: This DOES affect data flow. Reducing the range limits how far away combat events are detected.

Examples:
• SELF — Only your own character’s events. The distance slider is automatically greyed out since it’s not relevant.
• PARTY — Your group of 5. In ArcheAge, everyone in your raid column is considered your “party.” For example, spells like Sonic Wave that “remove negative effects from all party members” affect your column of 5, not the entire raid.
• RAID — All parties in the raid (all columns).
• GUILD — Only players matching your guild tag. A second guild tag won’t appear since it’s technically a different guild.

Adjusting these in-game filters may be preferable to disabling features in the app, as they provide finer control over what data is processed.
